item.text: {"chapter_reviews":[{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"Mostly separated. UN/OSCE/ICRC and ICC materials identify their procedural limits; the Bucha-brigade record expressly distinguishes public Ukrainian allegations from proven individual criminal responsibility. The ICC warrant is correctly not presented as a conviction. Residual risk: institutional findings and command authority must not be converted into proof that Putin ordered particular field crimes.","closed_system_silence":"High concern. Russian censorship, restricted access to Russian-controlled sites, unavailable prosecutor files, inaccessible operational directives, and possible non-public proceedings mean absence of identified investigations cannot establish that none existed. The narrowly framed OHCHR absence finding is the defensible formulation.","duplicate_reporting":"Material overlap exists within the OHCHR/UN ecosystem and between the initial grain record and later signing/renewal records. The same source-locator-claim facts are also represented under initial E/WEB IDs and ledger WD IDs, so the identifier crosswalk requires deterministic reconciliation. The bundled initial grain record should not be counted alongside its later separated copies.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Yes. The notebook searches and retains favorable/qualifying material: the security dispute and ceasefire baseline, NATO proposal limits, Istanbul negotiations, the Grain Initiative, Ukraine-side violations, Russia’s Olenivka inquiry request, and Russia’s asserted positions. Adverse evidence is substantially broader. Russian official negotiating and remedial records were pursued, although complete draft texts and internal records were not recovered.","missing_source_type":"For the principal remaining attribution risks, missing source types are authenticated Russian operational/command records, military-prosecutor or court files, contemporaneous Russian negotiating drafts and decision records, and auditable 2022 procurement/beneficial-ownership data. The notebook credibly explains why these are unavailable or inaccessible; their absence remains an interpretation and confidence constraint.","official_claim_independence":"Official Russian claims are used principally for Putin’s decisions, rhetoric, decrees, and later funding statements, not as independent proof of their truth. NATO and Ukrainian official accounts are also appropriately treated as party accounts and are qualified with UN, court, monitoring, humanitarian, dataset, and wire-report evidence where available. The claimed availability of NATO diplomatic alternatives still rests primarily on NATO’s account of its own proposals.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Moderate concern. The scale of public allegations after the invasion can increase apparent severity or repeat the same incidents. This is partly controlled by relying on OHCHR, the Commission, OSCE, ICRC, and UCDP rather than complaint volume; findings nevertheless remain incomplete because monitors lacked full access.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Addressed well. The notebook identifies the inherited Donbas conflict and ceasefire baseline, Putin’s formal and direct strategic authority, NATO-Russia distrust and negotiation proposals, Ukrainian resistance, Western support, sanctions, battlefield setbacks, and shared combat outcomes. Population and outcome measures are not treated as automatic personal attribution.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WD001","WD002","WD003","WD004","WD006","WD008","WD009","WD011","WD012","WD013","WD014","WD015","WD016","WD018","WEB-2B-C1-004","WEB-2B-C1-005","WEB-2B-C1-006","WEB-2B-C2-001","WEB-2B-C2-004","WEB-2B-C2-005","WEB-2B-C2-006","WEB-2B-C2-007"],"unresolved_risks":["No direct evidence of Putin’s knowledge of, or orders for, particular operational crimes or affiliated-force abuses.","No complete, officially attributable Russian and Ukrainian spring-2022 draft texts or proof of Putin’s final acceptance/rejection of each material term.","No public, independently checkable Russian prosecution, discipline, or private remedial order for the documented 2022 abuses.","No auditable evidence resolving whether military/procurement funding created patronage benefits or personal enrichment.","Later retrospective sources and post-period judicial actions must remain clearly tied to 2022 conduct rather than described as 2022 events."]},"chapter_id":"2B","defensible_evidence_estimate":29,"independent_source_family_estimate":20,"missing_themes":["2B.5: direct evidence of effective command/control over particular affiliated units, Putin’s knowledge of specific abuses, and corrective orders.","2B.7: complete contemporaneous Russian and Ukrainian draft texts and ruler-level evidence on final acceptance of a settlement.","2B.8: 2022 procurement, beneficial-ownership, and audited financial evidence capable of distinguishing wartime resourcing from patronage or personal enrichment.","2B.9: independently verifiable Russian investigative, prosecutorial, disciplinary, or remedial records, including any non-public-process limitation."],"substantive_issues":["The initial Black Sea Grain Initiative record bundles distinct July-signing and November-renewal events and locators; later records separately recreate those facts. Count only separated, non-duplicative claim units.","The notebook contains parallel E/WEB and WD identifiers for the same earlier source-locator-claim units. Reconcile to one stable global ID per fact before downstream use.","Some initial records provide a second URL inside a locator rather than a separate stable source-claim unit; that is insufficient for counting the second source independently.","The statement that Putin ‘presided over and publicly defended’ annexation lacks a direct cited Putin record in the retained unit; UN evidence supports the act and international response, while direct personal attribution should rest on a precise Putin source or authority-based responsibility.","The Al Jazeera brigade item is usable only as a carefully bounded account of a presidential commendation after allegations became public; it cannot establish unit culpability, prior knowledge, or a personal abuse order."]}],"global_findings":["Terminal review: research rounds were exhausted without full saturation; this is not a claim that the dossier is complete.","For the selected 2B lenses, the dossier has broad, period-fit evidence across direct decisions, legal/institutional findings, consequences, diplomacy, and contrary material. The strongest remaining limits concern operational attribution, private remediation, complete negotiation records, and financial-beneficiary evidence.","No additional continuation is requested because the remaining gaps are preserved as unresolved risks under the terminal instruction and the notebook documents credible access and source-availability limits."],"needs_continuation":false,"reviewer_summary":"Evidence is adequate for a qualified downstream assessment of the selected 2B lenses, provided duplicate identifiers and bundled grain records are reconciled and institutional findings are not overstated as personal orders. Residual attribution, access, and financial-motive gaps remain material for confidence and interpretation.","schema_version":"ruler_evidence_review_v1","selected_theme_ids":[]}
